source_en: Late close. Fixed the stall's freezer door.
Home after the late shift. Block scrubbed.
Back to sharpen the cleavers.
Checking the back door seals.
Gauze ration from the polyclinic. Two rolls.
Bartering meat at market. Protein is protein.
Back from the fence. Needed the sky.
Stall's empty. Nothing left to cut.
Looking for a bed that isn't grey.
Home from the tax inspectorate. Day shift.
New in town. Seeking market work.
Posing for the art institute portrait class.
Vegetarian society meeting. No meat in years.
Pension after forty years at the bakery.
Fainted at blood again. Seeing the doctor.
Inspector checking radiation safety protocols.
Coming from a wedding. I was flower boy.
Restocking my stall. Fresh deliveries daily.
Careful with the permit. My hands are always a bit… slick.
The bandages? Little accident at the shop. Don't stare.
The hunger isn't in my stomach anymore. It's in my teeth.
I feel the air touching my raw face through the gauze.
My papers. Sorry about the blood. Comes with the profession.
Hope you're not sick of me. I've been dying to see you.
Stop by later. I'll give you a 'cut'. Get it?
Try to stay plump, officer. It suits you.
Go on. The world's one big cold-storage anyway.
Solitary? My favourite kind of kitchen. Very private.
The walls look chewy. I'll tell you how they taste.
First clean cut I've been on the receiving end of…
Aw, and I was just starting to like your face.
Where are you coming from?
My market stall. Scrubbed the block, fixed the freezer door. Late shift.
Polyclinic for gauze, two rolls a week. Then the stall's back door seals.
The boundary fence. Wanted the sky. Nothing left at the stall to cut.
The meat plant on the river road. Day shift, good union job.
Polyclinic. Stitches out. The grinder only got me last month.
The burns ward. My face healed nicely since the kitchen fire.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My back, like every butcher's. The face itches under the gauze.
Sweating. The room goes dark when I stand. And hungry. Always hungry.
Hands shake since last week. Bad, with knives. I still cut straight.
Nothing. Twenty years lifting carcasses and not one sore back.
Healthy as a bull. Schoolboy blood pressure. I barely eat these days.
Steady, look. Sold the stall in spring. Haven't touched a knife since.
Ever notice how quiet the streets are at night? I love that.
Got a special cut waiting at the shop. Looking forward to it all day.
Hear the grinding? It doesn't stop. I've stopped trying to make it.
The hunger's gotten very specific lately. Hard to explain over a booth.
You look like you haven't slept, officer. Neither have I. Don't miss it.
Bandages are dry today. First time in a while. Testing a theory.
